slides.title: Context Managers & Resource Management Overview
slides.prompt: Context managers handle the precise allocation and release of resources (like file descriptors or network connections) using the 'with' statement. They guarantee proper cleanup even if exceptions occur during execution.

slides.title: Context Manager Setup Method
slides.prompt: Fill in the magic method name executed when entering a 'with' block to acquire resources.

slides.title: Exit Method Exception Suppression
slides.prompt: How can an __exit__ method prevent an exception that occurred inside a 'with' block from propagating upwards?
options: By returning True from the __exit__ method
By returning False from the __exit__ method
slides.correctAnswer: By returning True from the __exit__ method

slides.title: Contextlib Decorator Usage
slides.prompt: Fill in the decorator name from 'contextlib' used to turn a generator function into a context manager.

slides.title: Parameters of __exit__ Method
slides.prompt: Which three parameters must the __exit__ method accept besides 'self' to handle exception details?

slides.title: The With Statement Keyword
slides.prompt: Fill in the keyword used to bind the target object returned by __enter__ to a variable name.

slides.title: Multiple Context Managers Syntax
slides.prompt: Which syntax allows managing multiple resources simultaneously in Python 3.10+?
options: with (open('f1.txt') as f1, open('f2.txt') as f2):
with open('f1.txt') as f1 and open('f2.txt') as f2:
with [open('f1.txt') as f1, open('f2.txt') as f2]:
with open('f1.txt') as f1 ; open('f2.txt') as f2:
slides.correctAnswer: with (open('f1.txt') as f1, open('f2.txt') as f2):
